winner_analysis.why_it_won: A specific, funny number (“47 socks, I counted”) plus a familiar household pain: viewers recognize themselves within 2 seconds, and the UGC delivery feels like a review, not an ad.
winner_analysis.keep_unchanged: Everything after second 3: socks dumped on the bed, the magnetic click close-up, pairs coming out of the dryer, the 5 pairs for $29 offer and the quiz CTA.

variants.hook_visual: Close-up: a hand pulls a single sock out of the washer drum, peeks inside, and it's empty. Hollow drum sound.
variants.first_line: Every laundry day, one sock just... disappears.
variants.why: The most recognizable pain moment, the empty drum, raises a question the body of the ad answers.

variants.hook_visual: Kinetic type on black: a “Washer vs Me” scoreboard, the washer's score spins up fast, then a hard cut to the sock basket from the original.
variants.first_line: I started keeping score against our washing machine.
variants.why: A sports-style score builds intrigue and humor: viewers want to see how the game ends.

variants.hook_visual: Stock footage of a washer with simple motion-graphic eyes and teeth on top: the machine “chews” a sock for 2 seconds.
variants.first_line: Our washing machine is on a strict sock-only diet.
variants.why: Personifying the washer gives absurd humor that needs no shoot and begs to be shared.

variants.hook_visual: Same UGC footage, but for the first second she speaks quietly, closer to the camera, like a confession; soft light, kitchen behind her.
variants.first_line: Okay, confession: I've been secretly throwing out single socks for years.
variants.why: The confession format holds attention: viewers wait for what comes next and recognize their own habit.

variants.hook_visual: Full-screen text over a pile of socks: “Stop buying socks.” One second later, cut to her with the basket.
variants.why: A paradox from a sock brand stops the scroll; the body explains the problem is pairs, not quantity.

variants.hook_visual: The product first: two SockLock socks snap together at the cuff in slow motion with a loud click. Then cut to the basket.
variants.first_line: These socks literally cannot get separated.
variants.why: The mechanism is clear in one second; the loud sound stops people curious about how it works.

variants.hook_visual: Morning rush (stock): she digs through a drawer wearing one sock, the phone screen shows 7:52.
variants.first_line: It's 7:52 and I'm hunting for a matching sock. Again.
variants.why: The same pain in another context, the morning instead of laundry day, reaches people who never think about the washer.

variants.hook_visual: A detective board: sock photos, red strings between the washer, dryer and couch (simple motion graphics), then cut to the basket.
variants.first_line: I finally figured out where all our missing socks go.
variants.why: Promising an answer to an eternal question is a classic curiosity gap, and the body closes it.

warnings: H02 reuses the number “47” from the original. Keep it only if those are the UGC creator's real words.
H05 “Stop buying socks” is a paradox for a sock brand. Check that the transition to “So I switched to these” lands as a resolution, not a contradiction.
H06 shows the product before the pain: check that the cut to the pile of socks in the body doesn't confuse viewers.
